label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Bow Summit: not yet!
reports.comment: quick: Needs another storm. About 10HS at parking lot. 30HS in the middle of the roadside chutes

reports.title: Small pockets releasing
reports.comment: quick: Small pockets at ridgetop cracking and cross loaded gully released size 1 loaded by strong westerly.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Given the marginal conditions with minimal base, some nice deep turns were had and we received around 12cm of snow over about 4 hours, snow fall picked significantly up as we got back on the 93. Shooting cracks and some shingling on any loaded/steep terrain. Did not witness nor trigger any slides.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Went for a walk with low expectations and were pleasantly surprised with conditions. HS was highly variable, up to 80cm at tree line, average of 45cm overall. Skied 3 laps of the far lookers left tree runs. Skiing is possible only in sheltered/lee features. Had 1 run with no rock or tree strikes. Ventured up towards dogleg and skied a mellow peice of the fan but found a reactive layer down …

reports.title: First time out
reports.comment:
quick: This is my first time getting out un guided and I have limited knowledge so please take this in consideration when reading this less than technically eloquent report.

We started the day in the thick trees and made our way up on what seemed to be a supportive snow pack. There was a nice new layer of snow on top. When poking my pole to the earth, I could feel 3 layers: soft/crust/soft. Overa…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: snowpack: CTH22 SC ~30 down

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: snowpack: CTH22 SC ~30 down

reports.title: Ferris
reports.comment: quick: Gorgeous day out! Decided to check out the Ferris glacier. Approach in actually was reasonable and the canyon skiable however observed numerous small slab releases on some of the canyon exits points failing to ground. ( which could be dangerous if swept in the creek). Further up hard trail breaking through trees and as expected very thin to the glacier. Ferris ranged from 40-80 cm coverage …

reports.title: Observation side
reports.comment: quick: This zone needs more snow. Good for walking only. Travelling through the forest with -30cm and lots of deadfall was challenging both up and down. Open areas exposed to sun were sun crusted. breakable but not skiable. 1-2cm west facing and over 5cm south west facing. A lot of whumphing. We skied a north aspect of a gully where snow seemed ok but were hitting ground on most turns. 2300m: in s…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Conditions report from Bow Summit on 11/19/2023:
Firstly, I'll start with a disclaimer that I am very new to this and by no means a reliable expert in reporting backcountry conditions. I would welcome any feedback, tips or corrections. Secondly, some of this info may be already obvious to much of the group or anyone paying attention to weather, but I thought I'd share it anyway for those wh…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: I decided to head up to Bow Summit again and see how far our snowpack had improved since I was there. Honestly, I don't see it as improving much, but there are a few things to note, good and bad.

On average, there is about 35-40cm of snow. The deepest pocket I could find was just below 50cm. You could be walking on the ground in plenty of places, though. The snowpack has two lightly packed…

reports.title: No instability noted
reports.comment: quick: Dead calm at Bow Lake for a change. Approacefaround north end of Lake and up to C-Train on Crowfoot north buttress, no instability of any kind noted. We avoided punching straight up the middle of the bowl below the climb , instead linked rock outcroppings. Easy to stay on rock most of the way due to wind-stripped slopes.

reports.title: Pointless - ice
reports.comment:
quick: Cold leaving the car and around the lake where a breeze kept it feeling cold. We followed the shoreline trail as the lake wasn't frozen a week ago but there were plenty of skaters on the lake later. 

Thankfully there is a well established bootpack trail to follow because the bushwhacking is quite bushy at times.

Two parties ahead of us and two parties behind us today. Had to wait some tim…

reports.title: Bow Summit.
reports.comment: weather: We were on site for aprox 3 hrs.   There were Variable wind speeds below 25kph, most snow is knocked off the trees.   Some evidence of wind loaded slopes was evident,  Leeward side was on the NE aspect. Cloud cover was intermittent between mostly open to sun obscured.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Mostly went for a walk, observed the snowpack which was weak and shallow see snowpack.   Stayed on previously skied or very compact zones for the descent. / snowpack: Up to 45cm deep in places at TL.  This pack is quite weak and not very confidence instilling.  Rutshblock 5 down 30-35cm

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse - Core Shots Included
reports.comment:
quick: We turned around mid-way, due to gear issues so we did not complete the full traverse. The snow may be better on the North East side of Dolomite. 

On the up track, the snow is dry and sugary, and it does not provide any sort of base. 

About 30 cm of snow, but that is just enough to hide the rocks and roots, not enough to keep you from hitting them. Everyone in our group needs a new tune a…

reports.title: Threading the needle at Oxo
reports.comment:
quick: Puzzle/Oxo has seen some greater days, but still enough snow that has collected from the wind that allowed for some surprisingly good turns. Ranged from 10cm to 100+, but was able to avoid shark fin soup for most of the descent. One size 2 natural that looked relatively fresh off of the big rock wall to lookers left of Oxo

Would not have wanted to step into much steeper as saw some reactiv…

reports.title: A-Bow-t Time
reports.comment: avalanche: Multiple deposits from within 24hrs. 1 x occurred in between laps, was observed lookers right of the Stem couloir, sz 1 triggered likely from wind loading in steep, shallow rocky terrain. / weather: S-1

reports.title: Noseeum avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Large avalanche crown visible from roadside.

reports.title: Pow Summit!
reports.comment:
quick: It's been a long wait but it finally looks like touring season! Extremely deep pow day at bow summit, stayed in more mellow terrain & at treeline. / snowpack: Went to explore around bow summit, ski cut a number of steep convex rolls on the way up at and below treeline & got no results.
Dug a pit at treeline, 65cm snowpack, ECTP 12 failing 35cm down on a thick crust above base facets. Snow w…

reports.title: mosquito creek area
reports.comment:
quick: poked around the mosquito creek area and it's still early season out there.   the snowpack was 60-100 cm at tree line, 3/4 of which was unconsolidated (in non-exposed areas) storm snow overlaying a facet layer.  there was some slab development with a few shooting cracks in more exposed areas at treeline.

the snowpack wasn't supportive at all, which made for tough travel and a few shark bit…

reports.title: Give it Time
reports.comment:
quick: 3 or more slides mid storm took out most of the bowl
what was left was mostly very thin and/or windslab

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder Test Profile
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful day to be out on skis but still very early season conditions even with recent snowfall. The mountains look pretty well covered from the road as winds haven't blown the recent snow away yet, but the snowpack is mostly unsupportive and there are still many hazards at or below the surface...  Be wary and don't ruin your season by charging too hard in this thin snowpack!

reports.title: West Nile Tree Jail
reports.comment: quick: Skiing at treeline and in gladed areas was excellent with boot-top powder and no notable crust at any elevation. However, access and egress were both difficult. There were many small trees in the slide paths which interrupted otherwise pleasant skiing. We noticed several whumpfs on flat/mellow terrain at treeline. As expected, needs more snow.

reports.title: JP
reports.comment: quick: We saw one avalanche up above the treeline, the snow in the trees was a little wet

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: There was no rain crust from trailhead to treeline. Between 50 to 65 cms of snow. In open glades treeline there was 1 cm  sun-crust. On the ridge line by the burn there was definite wind crust and whumping.

reports.title: dolomite traverse pleasant surprise
reports.comment: quick: late start paired with no real objective for the day led to us settling on dolomite traverse since the day was beautiful, got up to a ridge near lake katherine and saw another group skiing a mellow but fun looking slope and decided to do some laps there instead. slopes skied were on NE aspects and stayed mellow. on our approach and egress, which was SW facing, several instances of whoompfin…

reports.title: Oxo/Puzzle - threading the needle
reports.comment: quick: Better than expected skiing, but had to be very selective on the line choice and ski the zones you’d probably want to avoid if it was any steeper. Main line was a mix of windslab to creamy turns. Snowpack ranged anywhere from 10 cm to 110 cm on the main slope, but avoided the vast majority of sharks. Snow pack was generally garbage at the bottom with what looked like depth hoar or buried su…

reports.title: Wapta Icefields - Dec 17, 2023
reports.comment:
quick: Wapta Icefields this weekend (Dec 17, 2023):

Started at bow lake around 7 am. Lake was frozen well enough. The travel upto the hut was decent except for the valley and bowl just below the hut. Coverage was marginal here with many rocks sticking out.

There was only one other party at the hut. Went past bow hut and on to the upper glacier towards Mount Gordon. The view was stunning. Can't b…

reports.title: Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Variable snow depths ranging from 40-120cm. Found deeper snow in higher regions. / snowpack: Variable snow depths in the region, from 50cm to 120cm observed. Lots of whumphing noted

reports.title: Treeline Profile on Jimmy Junior Bowl Ridge
A Little Lost in Little Italy
reports.comment: quick: Skiied Dolomite Traverse today. Cloudy with broken periods, S -1 for the majority of the day. Travel below treeline is heinous at best, much to be said for expert alder smashing skills. HS was 40-60 throughout the day, many sharks and thin to thick sections in the area. We attempted to branch out in the alpine, but were met with large settlements and dramatic whumpfs, so we quickly returned…

reports.title: Bow summit avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Great skiing in the E facing treeline chutes. Much more variable HS above. / incident: Skinned above a steep unsupported rock slab. The snow at the crown was the only significant wind slab we’d seen all day. Should’ve listened to my spidey senses about the conditions. Got too comfortable after doing great laps in the treeline chutes.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Skiing BTL is pretty good where you can find open areas to ski. Once you hit around 2000-2200 m is where things get pretty shitty. Big settlements and shooting cracks that would propagate up to 10m in unsupported areas. Crust not supportive up to 2200m can’t speak to anything above that because we didn’t go any higher. 50-70cms HS with the bottom 10-20cm mostly facets. Great spot for a walk…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Remote
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche was remote triggered from ridgetop. Audible wumph was heard and it released on a convex roll.

reports.title: Crowfoot pass / glades
reports.comment: quick: Day out to check out high five wall just passed crowfoot pass. Turned back for the glades due to Na activity and sheer lack of HS on skiable slopes in the alpine. Travel was mostly supportive . Skiing the glades was 60-80 HS, 15 cms of fist on supportive mid pack. / avalanche: Saw 3 Na on N/Ne aspects , one confirmed cornice slab (see picture) and 2 a lot more filled in but noticeable debri…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior bowl
reports.comment: quick: Jimmy Junior Bowl. 50 cm HS @ 2300m with basal facets but very supportive. Didn't punch through & no rock strikes. Thin wind skin on most slopes but couldn't feel it under the skis once you got up to speed. No settlements or whoomphing. Surprising good skiing but all the low hanging fruit had been skied. Freshies if you are willing to climb higher than everyone else. Heavily tracked out in …

reports.title: Puzzle peak
reports.comment: quick: Went up to puzzle peak. Beautiful sunny day with great views. Pretty warm in the sun, high of -1. No new avalanches in the area. Some older wind slabs on the upper slopes of Dolomite shoulder in thin loaded terrain. Skiing was not great but we went up to the ridge of puzzle and got some nice views. Also dug a pit and found a surprisingly supportive snowpack for the thin rocky terrain I dug …

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Took a stroll up jimmy junior - the area has seen a lot of traffic. All aspects we rode were crusty, tracked, and somewhat wind affected. Made for a mix bag of skiing. 

Dug a quick pit at 2180 meters - south east facing slope. Most noticeable result was a resistant planar failure on the facets at the bottom of the snowpack (70cms deep) on CT18. 

Otherwise, no other signs of instability.

reports.title: Grand daddy scout
reports.comment: quick: Went up to the lower slopes of Grand daddy to poke around and dig some pits. Thinking we would get a handle on the snowpack in the area and see how we felt. Surprised to see multiple groups heading into Grand daddy as we broke out of the trees. We saw 13 people at one point all heading up or in the line. Any hopes we had of skiing the line evaporated and we just dug some pits and watched th…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: About 60 cm of base but has snowed a fair amount since the 4th. Good riding but could still use a bit more snow to cover some trees. Weak layer that failed on 3 shoulder swings.

reports.title: Observation Peak observations
reports.comment: quick: Kept expectations low today, but got pleasantly surprised with some ankle deep supportive turns in the sub-alpine. Stayed away from wind slabs and stuck to low angle slopes. Exit through dense trees low down was doable thanks to supportive layers under foot. Overcast throughout the day with light flurries, temps between -7 and -2. Surface snow stayed dry.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: More snow than expected, snow was falling steadily all day and overall stable riding conditions. Some heavy sloughing from steep features.

reports.title: Puzzle ramp
reports.comment: quick: Found wind affected snow on the approach, however conditions got better with elevation. Still fairly thin in some spots, narrowly missing a few buried rocks on the way down

reports.title: Crystal ridge roadside
reports.comment:
quick: Sluffing was evident during the ski down, sharks were still out and about on steeper slopes and lee areas affected by wind.

Looking across the road above crowfoot would see sluff/ dry snow coming down the cliffs about once an hour during the day / weather: No snow blowing on ridge tops, air temps were around -14/15 degrees consistently at 2300-2600 meters over 3 hours / snowpack: ECTN 27, …

reports.title: Natural activity
reports.comment: avalanche: The avalanche in the photo occurred out of terrain, on the lookers right of the Grand Daddy couloir. Started as a small avalanche and entrained mass, triggering the basal layers of the snowpack. Parks Canada Visitor Safety drove the 93N and 93S highways today and observed evidence of natural activity in many areas. Slab, loose dry and deep persistent avalanches were observed, largely ou…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: 5 cm new, generally 80 cm snow depth with midpack support.  Travelling at treeline we had numerous whumpfs on the basal weakness.  Sudden collapse results on the surface hoar down 22 cm.

Ski pen on way up was around 30 cm.  Reasonably good skiing on the way down.   At treeline, some wind affect in the immediate lees where the skis sometimes sunk beneath, and we occasionally broke through t…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured up Crystal Ridge today. It was partly sunny and quite warm. Low to no winds. Once we got out of the tree line just below 2500 m we heard two loud whoomps on the wind affected, SW facing, low angle slopes. Decided to turn around at this point. While walking above a convex feature shooting cracks appeared in a ca 5 m radius below.

reports.title: Whumph on Helen’s Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Below and at treelike had decent powder for skiing. Alpine was extremely wind affected. As we approached one of the higher ridges we heard a big whumph as the snow below us gave way. It created a crack along the length of the whole slope with a gap of about one inch. We made it back down to the tree line and had a great run out the trees.

reports.title: Bow Hut to Mt.Gordon
reports.comment: quick: Our group was at the Bow Hut on Friday, January 19 - Sunday, January 21.  Conditions on the skin track across Bow Lake and the canyon were fine with the larger than usual damp spots.  The approach to the hut after the canyon required additional route finding due to a lower snow pack.  The moraine field below the hut had lots of exposed rocks. This made the ski in/out a little more challengi…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Skied around the Crystal Ridge area today. Witnessed a small remote triggered size 1 above tree line, along with several whumphs and shooting cracks at tree line.

Snowpack was about 75cm at tree line, where we dug a pit - about 25cm of new snow sitting on top of 50cm of facets to ground. CT test showed nothing but a crumbly column. 

Skiing was mediocre at best, but a nice day with little …

reports.title: Facet-lanches and wind slabs
reports.comment:
quick: Lots of wind affected snow at treeline and above at Bow Summit. A test pit to investigate the stiff (pencil +) wind slab above the South Chutes gave:

CTM 11 (SC) down 40cm on large facets
ECTP 12 down 40cm on FC 3

These pit results reinforced our decision to avoid the recently loaded chutes.

I also cut some full depth loose/dry avalanches out of a steeper sheltered slope below treeline. …

reports.title: Funnel of Death
reports.comment: quick: We brought a 30m rad line to ski FOD top down. The cornice is the size of bus or a semi atm so a 30m rap would not be enough. My partner found an entrance 30 meters to skiers right where we did not have to rappel in. Snow in the top panel was affected by wind but had many spots to take cover and set up a belay in case we needed to ski cut it. Middle section was not skiable when we went (too…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak Avalanche Activity
reports.comment: avalanche: First photo is a small sz 0.5 natural slab avalanche we encountered at tree line. We stopped our ascent at tree line, but a solo skier passed us and kept going up into the alpine. When we got to our transition zone after a mellow run in the trees, we looked back up and saw two avalanches, probably sz 1-1.5, so we went back up the same way to see if the lone skier was OK. We could clearl…

reports.title: Wind slab slide at Bow Hut
reports.comment: quick: An update on our trip to Bow Hut.  We experienced a small slide on our ski out from Bow Hut.  The normal ski out route didn’t seem like a good option due to exposed rocks and poor snow coverage.  This lead our group to select a line to the skier left which lead us to the top of a bench above the lower creek.  We had a couple of steep chutes to select and felt we had selected the one that wa…

reports.title: Bow Summit Area
reports.comment:
quick: TP @2350m East Asp. 30deg slope. HS 105cm
CTE (8, 10) SP down 15cm
CTM (13, 15) SC down 55cm on FC above Crust. 

Looks like some folks had some decent turns today around Bow summit on lower angle slopes. Some wind effect and windslabs above 2275m. Our high point was 2350m. Interface above the Arctic Facets was interesting. Definitely enjoyed the warmer temps. / snowpack: TP @2350m East Asp…

reports.title: Bow headwall
reports.comment: quick: No wind affect BTL in bow lake region and approach to pointless gully. No recent Na observed. Foot penetration to ground in approximately 60 to 80 cm pack. Skiing BTL in this region would be ‘interesting’.  With the warmer temps and new snow, there is a somewhat hidden slush pit halfway along bow lake. Take care with your skins.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Went up to Crowfoot Glades. Stayed on mellow slopes on skiers left in the trees. Surprisingly no wind crust. Riding was good but got worse near the base. Due to the forecast we made conservative choices and stayed away from overhead / avalanche: Witnessed a cornice failure on the approach to Bowcrow causing a 1-2 size sluff avalanche with about 100 m runout. We made the decision to stay awa…

reports.title: Cirque Peak Centre Rib
reports.comment: quick: Reasonable skiing today up on the Cirque Forepeak with the ACC BITS group. Challenging ski conditions below treeline due to lack of snow. Alpine skiing was wind effected and crusty, best skiing was at treeline. No instabilities like whumphs or shooting cracks were observed despite breaking trail for most of the day. Heard 1 avalanche from a distance, likely from the Crowfoot North / Bow Lak…

reports.title: No-Turn Ski Tour Molar Pass South
reports.comment: quick: Skinned towards Molar Pass South thru the Mosquito Valley.   Weather was cloudy, dry and about +2 at 10am as we started.  We noted loose/wet sluffing from the Nooseum ridge.  We both noted a couple shooting cracks while moving just past the fork/sign, towards Molar South.  On our return exit wet mist began which turned to light rain by about 4pm, we both noted and discussed the increased te…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Mixed precipitation at Bow Summit this morning created challenging snow and avalanche conditions in the field. Several Na to sz 2 were witnessed off Crowfoot Mtn. with heavy, wet snow to 2300m.
TP @2,200m revealed a CTV (SP) and ECTP5 dn 40 on FC 2.0mm. HS 110. Snowpack is very weak and facetted. / avalanche: Several Na LW to sz 1.5 also observed in the area. / weather: 1.5C temp taken at 1…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak Drainage Avalanches
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed all three avalanches naturally release between 1220-1235.

reports.title: Natural Avalanche Cycle on 93N
reports.comment: avalanche: During our field day in the Bow Summit area, a wide spread natural cycle was observed at all aspects and elevations. Deep persistent and persistent slabs at treeline and in the alpine up to size 2.5. And loose wet avalanches at treeline and below treeline up to size 1.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: A keenness to stretch the legs and see what was happening in the snowpack had us out at Dolomite Shoulder for a wander. Travel conditions below treeline could do with a little work, with an unsupportive crust if brave enough to stray off the skin track. We observed numerous avalanches on all aspects, likely stemming from the natural avalanche cycle over the last few days. This included a sz…

reports.title: Bow Summit S Glades
reports.comment: quick: Went to Bow Summit today to poke around and maybe get a little skiing in (kept hopes low). At 10:00AM at the parking lot temperature was 1C with consistent light snow. Headed to the Bow South Glades and noticed wind affected snow and melt/freeze crust all along the ridge with strong winds and air temp of -2C. Glade skiing was better than expected! Snow was varied between crust and soft on t…

reports.title: Excellent Parkway Conditions
reports.comment: quick: Excellent day of dust-on-crust skiing near bow summit yesterday. The melt/freeze crust with powder on top made for very consistent, fast, and fun skiing. It was the best day of skiing I've had this season. Very weak snowpack in thin rocky areas, but much better in thicker snowpack areas, and down below treeline.

reports.title: Near Miss Bow Lake
reports.comment:
quick: Start out 5:45 a.m. from the lodge and 1km in, while crossing Bow Lake, went through the ice. Didn't have enough time to feel snow conditions but was asked to share a MIN to spread awareness around the instability of lake crossings after the warming period.

More specifically what happened - we were crossing the usual spot heading towards Bow Hut, maybe 50 meters off shore. Lots of fresh tr…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior bowl
reports.comment:
quick: 15 cm of dry powder on the surface with no wind effect made for good skiing. Guessing that south facing slopes got a thin suncrust on them today.

The Feb 3 melt-freeze crust is under this new snow and was supportive on skis but not boots. No new avalanches observed today.

reports.title: Puzzle Ramp
reports.comment:
quick: We skied 1 lap on Puzzle Ramp run. Snowpack is about what we're finding in most places on the 93n, shallow but when you can find a good crust it works out for skiing. 

The snow on ground is still depth hoar/facets, mid pack looks to be mixed forms trending towards rounds, and above that is the crust and the snow that fell recently. HS is variable, we saw ground in places (BTL and TL) and m…

reports.title: Not bad riding in bluebird conditions
reports.comment: quick: Loads of hoar frost on the top layer, and a crust now buried from the warm cycle last week made breaking trail interesting. We toured up to the treeline and observed some slide residue on the other side of the valley, up to size 1.5. Riding down was deep powder but the buried crust made things interesting.

reports.title: Bow Lake North shore
reports.comment: quick: We climbed Pointless Gully and on the way out saw several debris deposits from today, one of them fairly large. A few of the slides occured at or below treeline, all on S aspects.

reports.title: Bow falls
reports.comment:
quick: Bow Falls today! Lake has refrozen, and there was no issues crossing it. Very minimal snow on the slopes below bow Falls, two of our party of three slipped on water, polished slabs under the fresh snow, so take care. The wind has really played with the snow sometime snow height was as little as a few centimetres or sometimes up to perhaps 40 cm where it is crusty. 
The approach pitches are …

reports.title: Recent Avalanche Debris covering Bow Summit skier tracks
reports.comment:
avalanche: Some of my numbers are estimates.  I'm confident in the estimated size and start /end elevations of the runout. Recent weather was partly cloudy with a rapid temperature drop followed by a rapid temperature rise.
Start zone terrain was non-skiing extreme but mid level  area and base runout area were prime skiing terrain.

reports.title: Unnamed peak north of Mount Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment:
avalanche: We spotted an avalanche in the north part of Mount Jimmy Simpson (see map) on Saturday, Feb 10th around 11 am. 
It looked quite fresh so it probably happened not long ago, probably one of the previous days.

We noticed ski tracks in runout zone (marked by red arrows), luckily ski tracks were in and out meaning skier(s) were not buried.

Probably skier(s) crossed the avalanche path not l…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Best ski day of the year for me up at Cirque Forepeak!  TONS of settlements and shooting cracks in the alpine on the way up.  Every 10-15m while breaking trail in the alpine.  We kept our angle of ascent mellow and picked a reasonable way to the top with good routefinding.  We tagged the true summit of the forepeak from the local highpoint, which we protected with a rope.  Used a 240cm slin…

reports.title: Spring-like Conditions at Puzzle
reports.comment:
quick: Had an amazing day out on Puzzle Peak (as I'm sure a lot of the bow valley had this week!) While tracked in, old tracks were no issue and there was still a ton of room to play. 

Pin location is approx. where we decided to dig a pit. Total snow pack came to around 3.5 feet. about 3 cm of new snow on top of 1 cm crust to another chunk of new snow and another crust, with somewhat consolidated…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: We toured the Dolomite Circuit, and skied Helen Ridge and Puzzle Ramp along the way.
Helen Ridge was nice creamy snow, didn’t feel the crust while skiing. Puzzle Ramp was thin and sharky.

The day started overcast, and cleared to few clouds around 1200. Temps ranging from -8 to -1. Winds calm to light. 
Feb 3 crust was present throughout, with 5-20 recent/transported snow on top. Some visib…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: While traversing on top of a narrow alpine ridge feature a member of our party remote triggered a sz. 2-2.5 avalanche that ran roughly 400-500m downslope, with a crown that varied between 10-60cm and had a propagation width of roughly 25m. We then pushed a bit further and intentionally triggered a second slightly smaller avalanche on the adjacent feature. Needless to say the snow was to…

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Skied some laps on the burns at Helen shoulder. Ride quality was excellent, with 5-10cm of snow on top of a supportive crust. Still plenty of fresh tracks to be had. 

On south facing solar aspects we found a widespread crust 1-2cm thick down 5-10cm. Crust was supportive to skis. Underneath that crust were a number of other thin crusts interspersed with mostly faceted snow. With a thick cru…

reports.title: Ramp and Quartzite peak
reports.comment: quick: Headed toward Mosquito mountain but was looking a little thin. It's lower south slopes were breakable Sun crust on facets. So we headed towards Ramp and Quartzite.  We had good skiing on both slopes. The top 50 m of both peaks were rocky.  The faces both had between 30cm to 100cm of snow.  10-20 cm of light powder of a supportive crust over bottomless facets.  In shallow areas the crust was…

reports.title: Cirque Summit and North Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: The first two photos are from the Cirque Forepeak Skier remote and Skier controlled avalanches that we reported Tuesday. The third photo is looking down the couloir after cleaning out a slab avalanche before skiing. 

Rope beta, bring minimum two 50m ropes in order to make the full rappel in one go. There is some tatt on a horn that can be used as a mid anchor but there isn’t much room at i…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Conditions overall were quite good. I noticed no signs of instability or settlement. There is some quality powder on the north aspect moraines.

reports.title: Flour
reports.comment: quick: Great outing in perfect weather. Got up high topping out above flower coulior. Signs of wind slabs forming with moderate blowing snow. We found stubborn loaded pockets 10-50cm. We managed to pop one, running fast but fizzling out before the bottom. We founs Good skiing where sheltered from wind and sun

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: We skied flower couloir today as a party of 5. 1 other party of 4 followed our bootpack. It was -22 at the car at 9am, and -2 at 1pm when we returned. The bootpack was made up of variable snow, mostly blown in sluff sitting over the supportive temperature crust. The very top ~30 meters had thin coverage, we exposed a couple rocks and this was right at the elevation where that temperature cr…

reports.title: Peyto access to Peyto Hut, Rhondda,  Bow Exit
reports.comment: quick: Peyto access was OK, with a skis-off creek crossing and a bootpack up the creek onto the moraine we could have likely avoided by taking the summer trail up the right side. Peyto glacier skin track was ok from left to right, then around the crevasses to peyto hut. Rhondda summit without taking skins or skis off, then skied down East ridge as north face has open crevasses. Bow and Peyto glaci…

reports.title: Puzzle
reports.comment: quick: Right around 1 we started noticing the snow getting heavier as we approached the upper alpine. This stopped around 2550m where we began noticing it was soft again. By the time we made our descent, a slight sun crust had formed at lower elevations. Overall conditions were good, no noticeable instabilities. Most areas had a crust 10-20cm down, with a shallow snowpack overall.

reports.title: No Noseeum
reports.comment: quick: Some of the worst, (loudest) skiing I’ve done in a long time. Virtually every inch of the valley was washed out, covered in rock hard debris. S facing couloirs we’re all washed to ground and not skiable, all but one far lookers left N facing couloir was washed to ground where we boot packed up ~250ft and made the transition for some rather variable turns. Not recommended!

reports.title: Mosquito Mountain
reports.comment:
quick: We had stable if wind and sun affected slopes up to the nob at treeline.

Approaching the summit ridge, we curved around the outside of the mountain. Going up, first skier had whumping and a Crack. Second skier had no reaction.

Skiing down, both skiers were well spaced. Both skiers had shooting cracks, with top layers of snow moving. Lower layers held, and no avalanche occurred.

reports.title: Bow Falls Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: On our way up to the ice climb we experienced storm slabs. Ice axe spike was causing small shooting cracks. Eventually a 7 meter crack occurred. I dug a quick hand shear that required a lot of force to pull. It was non planar on the storm slab interface with facets below, 20cm down. We continued 1.5 meters to the right of the left shooting crack when the entire right slope collapsed with cr…

reports.title: Hidden bowl area
reports.comment:
quick: Quite day out at hidden bowl area. Only seeing two other people all day. 

Hidden bowl had a recent size 1/2 avy which was likely from cornice collapse on the new storm slab. ( see photo) we did not venture far in the bowl but had excellent snow. 

Then skied the Xmas trees to the north to the hwy and found 20-40 cm of new snow. Excellent. Cracking and whumps found at Treeline. Certainly he…

reports.title: Bow Summit Natural Cycle
reports.comment:
quick: Large natural cycle on East aspects. Windslab at alpine  ridgeline up to size two. Some large loose dry. Kept it mellow. Lots  of whumpfing and settlements / snowpack: HS 140 SE Aspect 2300m
CTE - 30 cm storm slab 
CTM 110cm on crust RP 
Overall not confidant in steep terrain kept it mellow and enjoyed some sunshine

reports.title: Remote trigger 1.5 on crowfoot roadside chute #3
reports.comment: quick: We decided to park at crowfoot glacier viewpoint and skin down to crowfoot glades as we didn’t want to park too much into the roadway with accumulated snow. Started the day breaking trail and doing a lap down the glades. After moving to the ridge and checking out the chutes from above. We decided on roadside chute #3 as it’s fairly wide, has safe areas and is the most tree’d of the cutes to…

reports.title: Laps at Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: We went out to check the conditions at Bow Summit and had a few amazing laps in great powder. We had some whumpfing heading up, but didn't notice any cracks. We had no skier triggered avalanches and saw no recent natural avalanches, but visibility was limited higher in the alpine.

reports.title: Touchy Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Toured up a ridge separating 2 bowls on the east aspect of dolomite shoulder. Remote triggered 2 size 2 avalanches in the adjacent bowls on the way up. Trail breaking wasn't too bad, with about 15, sometimes 25cm ski pen. Skied back down the ridge for some mellow but good quality turns. On the way back up for our second lap, our track had been noticeably filled in by the wind in some places…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Quite an uneventful day.  -20 C at truck heading in with very light wind and mainly cloudy.  Back at the truck it was -10 C at 2:30 PM and little wind as well.  High in Alpine to the south west you could see some wind and snow transport.

Skied some very short laps on mellow terrain to get a feel for things.  Both on climb and descent there were no observations of instability despite report…

reports.title: Puzzle ramp
reports.comment: quick: Puzzle ramp, saw the slides on dolomite shoulder reported in the min from yesterday and included some pictures of those. Also saw a natural slide on the north margin of puzzle ramp. Lots of whumphs (at least a dozen) throughout the day but stuck to low angle terrain and didn't get anything to move

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Great skiing in west Nile area today. Our group stuck to the trees and didn’t venture past tree line. Great snow but did notice some whumpfing on the ski down in the steeper sections.

reports.title: Observation Glades
reports.comment: snowpack: While we weren't on slopes over 30 degrees we could feel whoomphing and see/feel the settlement knock trees bombs out of the trees up to 20m away. Observed numerous avalanches on nearby slopes. All features over 30 deg. slid/avalanched.

reports.title: Bow Summit Ski
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the lower east facing gullies of Bow Summit, from the high ridge line before getting out in the open exposed faces. 
Dug a small pit on a mostly East facing slope (80 degree bearing), 30 degree slope angle. Result:

HS: 200cm snow depth
CTE8 non-planar collapse 12cm down (storm snow)
CTH26 non-planar collapse on facets 125cm down. 

Pretty solid results, no major notes of instabilitie…

reports.title: Cirque forepeak avalanche
reports.comment:
avalanche: 200m wide slide lookers left of cirque forepeak facing the road.
Experienced consistent whumping in the  flatter area below... Stayed on very mellow terrain. 
Dead phones, no pics.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek area - Profile NE aspect
Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Took a peak up looker's right of the natural avi debris before a large settlement turned us quickly around. Did a few laps off Crystal Ridge, about 10cm of soft wind slab on top of dense wind slab that was supportive to skiier weight with sastrugi at ridgetop.

Several whumpfs and settlements throughout the day when breaking trail, no shooting cracks. Afternoon sun started soaking the snow …

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment:
quick: Went up Observation sub peak south ridge and skied down the Cirque/ Observation col. Most steep slopes in the area had slid during or after the last avalanche cycle. 
One newer slab  observed (24-48 hrs old) off Cirque sub peak north aspect between 2400 m and 2250. 
The alpine is heavily wind affected and wind scoured on windward slopes.

reports.title: Windy Oxo
reports.comment:
quick: Solid day at Oxo, though very very windy. Skin track was disappearing between laps. Wind slab wasn’t too stiff at start of day but was absolutely cranking wind from the SW and expect that this will develop into stiffer slabs. Good day in the sun in low angle terrain. Sun crust was developing and expect will be bad after tonight’s freeze

Big whumpf on the skin track on way out in non conseq…

reports.title: Windy Oxo
reports.comment:
quick: Solid day at Oxo, though very very windy. Skin track was disappearing between laps. Wind slab wasn’t too stiff at start of day but was absolutely cranking wind from the SW and expect that this will develop into stiffer slabs. Good day in the sun in low angle terrain. Sun crust was developing and expect will be bad after tonight’s freeze

Big whumpf on the skin track on way out in non conseq…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades resort
reports.comment:
quick: Went and skiied around crowfoot glades, lots of groups out. Pretty good skiing if you found a fresh line.

 Saw 5 natural avalanches come down. 4 above the glades, coming off the bowcrow cliffs. 1 off crowfoot mountain above the ice fall. All looked to be cornice failures. Lots of wind coming off the wapta. The cornices would hit the fan causing the new snow slab to run half way down the fa…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades Outing
reports.comment: quick: Sighting of natural avalanches

reports.title: Gutentight Couloir
reports.comment: incident: Party of 2 climbed up the Gutentight Couloir then while descending the upper person was hit by a large sluff (?) which carried them approximately 350 m through the choke of the couloir and out onto the fan below.  Arm and back injuries and helmet smashed. Avalanche was probably a size 2 that ran a long distance in Extreme terrain.

reports.title: Natural avalanche off Vulture Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: Fairly large size 2+ natural avalanche occurred on the Vulture Peak headwall above the Bow Hut approach. Debris ran down to valley bottom and crossed a portion of the recent approach track to Bow Hut. Appeared to fail on a deep weak layer. Unsure about the trigger.

reports.title: Mt Gordon N face
reports.comment: quick: Went up Mt Gordon and skied the N facing ramp between the 2 summits. Great ski quality. No sluffing on the convex roll half way down. No sounds of instability or new Na activity. Still some big holes up there where I’d not seen any last 2 winters! We probed between 120- 200cm HS on the glacier

reports.title: March 12 skier remote 2.5
reports.comment: avalanche: Above peyto hut on moraine adjacent to glacier. Triggered from flat bench approaching glacier. Heard a soft whumpf. All details are estimated. Suspect crown was 50-150cm. There was a fair bit of the slope that also wrinkled but didn’t run.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek
reports.comment: avalanche: While skiing out of West Nile’s, heard a large rumble that last many seconds. Looked around, but couldn’t see much as we were in heavy trees. Once we got to a clearing below tree line, we looked up and saw a size 3 natural avalanche had occurred and propagated across the entire slope (100+ metres). No one was involved, timing was approximately 1:00 pm when the avalanche occurred.

reports.title: Observation Avalanches
reports.comment: quick: Skied Oxo Puzzle Thursday March 14th. Decided to head out for the last day of cooler weather for a while. Surface snow was moist and heavy but still managed to get a few good turns in on low angle slopes. Top 5-10cm was moist almost to all elevations and aspects by 4pm. Numerous wet loose up 2650m, less than size one, observed all day. Observed older (48-72hours) size 2+ avalanches on N-E a…

reports.title: Mt Gordon
reports.comment: quick: Woke up early and headed up to ski Gordon. Refreeze resulted in a 10cm thick crust made for quick travel. Saw lots of Sz 2-3 slabs from the recent warm up. Dug a pit at TL, N aspect and got CTM20 (SP) down 74cm on Facets overlying the Feb 3rd MFC. Snowpack is definitely hardening up but still a bit spooky. Probed 170-205cm on the glacier. Good skiing an even some powder found above 2600m, s…

reports.title: Pleasant change of plans
reports.comment: quick: Quick - Much more snow than expected lead to a change in plans. Skied flower couloir and 4 laps in the glades. Average of 15cm of fist over the crust (supportive to ski) up to 2300 meters. At 2400 meters and above Crust was not present on the north quarter. Top of flower(stem) was seeing up to 30 cms of fist on 4f trending 1F until basement facets and depth hoar (fist) . Slough management w…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied Helen shoulder, stuck to solar aspects, seeing 5-15cm of new dense snow on top of a widespread burly supportive crust. Observed no cracking or slab development, except minimal cracking on isolated NE lees. The new snow seems to be bonding well to the crust, we couldn't get much to move or entrain, though we kept away from very steep terrain or lee slopes. Ski quality good, but you can…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Headed up helen shoulder today. Our goal was to explore both north and south facing aspects.

1- Before ripping the skins we heard from across the valley a loud sound and watched a decently sized avalanche rip north aspect off Bowcrow Peak. Clouds covered the top section preventing us to see much and the debris landed in the shade and was hard to distinguish during the rest of the day.
Phot…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior
reports.comment:
quick: Headed up to Jimmy Junior 

Travel between 2000-2250m was difficult with 10-15cm of variable sun affected snow sitting on top of a thick crust. Travel after 2250m improved quickly but even on polar aspects snow was moist by 11:00. 

Snow pit at 2300m 

E Asp, Alp, HS 175cm
Results 
ECTP 17 down 75 on facets 

We observed numerous solar releases off of Jimmy junior up to size 0.5. 


Ski qua…

reports.title: Mount Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment: quick: Skied Mount Jimmy Simpson: 10-30cm of soft(F) new snow sits over the March 20th crust. This new snow became moist on solar aspects up to 2750m by 13:00, with some roller balling observed. Winds calm to ridgetop, with light W winds and some wind effect on the summit, no evidence of windslab. We saw evidence of wet loose and wet slab avalanches from the past week up to size 2 on solar aspects…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Amazing day out at crowfoot today. 30cms of fresh snow on top of a supportive layer made for great skiing.  Dug a pit on chute 1 that revealed negative ECT test, although we were eventually able to pull off a large block after the test about 90cm down, presumably on the early Feb layer, resistant planar. HS was 190cm. 

Then rode 3 laps of the glades, awesome skiing in the sun with buttery …

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: 10-20 cm of fresh fluffy snow sitting on a crust. As the temperature increased, the snow became heavy and wet. We had some whumpfs on the shallow snowpack on the SW facing slope of Cirque Forepeak. We turned around and lapped the treeline instead.

Midday, we heard what sounded like a large avalanche in the direction of Bowcrow. 

On our way back, we observed a few 0.5 wet slab avalanches s…

reports.title: Ramping it up
reports.comment: quick: Skied ramp peak, travel was very easy down-low in valley. Lapped 2 north facing mini features that remained dry snow (20 of fist). Anything solar that was under 2600 meter was moist to the crust , crust averaged 10-15 cms (very supportive) with moist snow below to ground at tree line where sun packed punch on true south. Ramp peak itself (2600 and above) stayed dry with a very light wind. 2…

reports.title: West Nile north slide path
reports.comment: quick: Sun crust under 10-20cm snow made for okay but not great skiing. Compression test showed no fractures, did not experience any instabilities while skiing. Feb3rd crust and basal facets present but didn’t cause issues. Other groups went up into the alpine with no problems from what I could tell. Overall a nice sunny day out but area will remain pretty tracked until more snow.

reports.title: Puzzle Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Great day out at puzzle peak! It was -10 at the car starting out but the alpine got warm with the heat day. By 2pm the surface started looking more wet and the snow was snowballing up more. 

There was 15-20 cm of light snow on top of a supportive crust which made for great skiing up high. A thin sun crust started to develop in sunny areas around 2500 m and below.

We noticed some recent sl…

reports.title: Mt Rhondda (Wapta area)
reports.comment: quick: Mt Rhondda (Wapta Conditions Photos), March 23-25, 2024. Day 1 skied into Bow Hut with a noon start, canyon had great coverage with minimal overhead remaining, easy travel. Weather better than expected with clearing skies, ended up bluebird. ~15cm of fresh powder atop the solar crust, didn't ski but ski quality would have been excellent. Saw some natural avalanches but pretty isolated, thin…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Amazing snow (up to waist deep powder). We were one of two parties up today so there is lots more to be skied. / avalanche: Watch the runout of two dry loose size 1s coming from higher up, coming off of the crowfoot glacier.

reports.title: Mt. Jimmy jr.
reports.comment:
quick: Very good conditions out there. But we saw many red flags in the higher alpine.

A strong supportive layer was present almost all the way to the summit where you couldn't punch a pole through, which made for some slippery situations, but we made it up without ski crampons. The new snow made it pretty workable for up tracking.  And the turns were some of the best of the year from the ground …

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Numerous small avalanches running from the rocks/cliffs along looker's right of the bowl. Most of the steep slopes along the looker's right have slide. Looked like at least a 30cm crown. Avalanche debris piled up on the edge of the main slope. Recent - the debris was not covered by the recent fresh snow - probably caused by solar heating on Thursday afternoon. Saw one spin drift avalanche o…

reports.title: Remote Slab on Mt Habel
reports.comment: quick: Interesting isolated slab release (remote) on an east aspect just below the summit ridge of Mt Habel. A group skied the slope earlier that morning and must have set it off. We didn't dig a pit but noted 30cm storm snow on a very icy (suncrust) slab, 35º east aspect. A 100m further down the slope at about 25º we measured 50cm storm snow on a suncrust but hand shears indicated a much better b…

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Observation Sub Peak Tour: Late start due to a rainy morning. Above 2200m, rain effect dissipated and 4-10 cm of now snow sits atop or continues to build the fresh windslabs below. Lots of natural activity observed. One Sz 2, suspect cornice failure of Jimmy Simpson observed at 1015, and several size 2 Na came down off cirque north bowl and the cirque forepeak couloirs during the day. On th…

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Flower couloir attempt. Turned around due to very reactive hand shears on the fan. / snowpack: Partway up flower couloir fan did a couple of hand shears which failed during isolation. Failure layer was mix of facets and rounds between 2 weak crusts. Dug a hasty pit and got CTM2(sudden planar) down 23 on the same layer and PST 22/100 end down 23 as well. Bailed after filling in the pit.

reports.title: Size 1 Storm Slab on Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: Triggered a size 1 storm slab in couloir feature while skiing across at ridge top. We had already skinned across this feature and triggered the avalanche while skiing back down. Our track was just below ridge crest as there was a cornice on the other side of the ridge. The avalanche failed on a melt freeze crust. It was a whiteout so we couldn’t observe the runout length.

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Fairly solid snow in Flower today, although it would have been nicer if we had got there an hour earlier, as on the second half of the ascent, the snow started warming up quite rapidly. Pinwheels were observed and lots of sluffing along the descent. Overall, fairly stable base underneath the top 10cm / snowpack: ECTX

reports.title: Cirque and St Nick
reports.comment:
quick: April 4/24: Cirque peak North Couloir: Moderate to strong ridgetop winds and several sz 1.5 Na observed in steep terrain. One new sz 2 in cirque north bowl. Whumphs and cracking in shallow Rocky alpine areas. Cirque north glacier had 20cm of dry schnoodleable snow, HS was 280 on probing.

April 5/24: Quick recce up the Wapta via Bow Lake. 15-20cm dry snow in AM becoming moist by afternoon. …

reports.title: North Face Natural
reports.comment: avalanche: Natural avalanche, likely on April 5.  Went to ground, started from just below the cliff band and ran at least 200m.

reports.title: Balfour hut area
reports.comment:
quick: Spent a day exploring around Balfour hut. Ascended to wind lip on this outlier of Mt Gordon, but got 2 large whumphs near the summit. We turned around at 2870m and skied the mellow glacier and then headed back to the hut. 

Spoke to another party in the parking lot who attempted Balfour, but had a large cornice failure while on the ridge, which turned them around. 

Generally good travel co…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Good coverage in the creek and the lake is still in great shape.  Crusty skinning to base of glacier but great pow on the glacier with a base of 200cm. Down drafting winds in the morning off the glacier but light to moderate Ne winds.  Sun came out for 30 minutes and softened up the snow on the south side of little crowfoot. Remote triggered a temperature slab on a south east facing slope 1…

reports.title: Hector and Wapta
reports.comment:
quick: Out for past 3 days poking around classic Rockies objectives. Notable improvement in stability and travel conditions compared to last week.

April 9/2024: Mt Hector. Poor visibility prevented us from ascending up the headwall. Due to the poor vis, we probed a lot of our uptrack and noted highly variable snow depth from 100-300+. One snow bridge in was found with a ~140cm bridge which indica…

reports.title: Mount Jimmy jr. lap
reports.comment: quick: Skied jimmy jr. via 2nd lookers left gully . Sporty travel in the gully , Not recommended for route choice if your looking for something easy. In the alpine travel was good seeing average of 15 up to 25 of f+ / 4 finger wind slab on top of laminated crust / march 20th (very supportive) .Only small pockets that were reactive at ridge top but on the east slope itself was unreactive and good w…

reports.title: Crowfoot/little crow
reports.comment: quick: Skied crowfoot mountain and little crowfoot. Skied off true summit of crowfoot with thinner snowpack along ridge but decent travel . On slopes below ridge average of 15 cms of 4f unreactive wind slab on top of supportive crust, Good skiing. Heard a couple whumpfs in the moraine complex coming up on leeward steep rolls but no cracking. Travel was great throughout day no ski cramps needed.  1…

reports.title: Bow Hut area
reports.comment: avalanche: Trying to save time, my partner I took a bit more risk than should have and skied the ramps down the N.E. side of St. Nicholas toward Bow hut. We did see other tracks of St. Nicholas off the summit ridge that didnt trigger windslab so we gave it a shot. Lower down around 2555m I tried to ski cut feature with thin Pencil hard windslab.  In picture going from lookers left to right, made i…

reports.title: Mistaya Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Long trip up to Mistaya mountain via Peyto hut, summit push on day one, skied out via bow hut day 2. Good travel conditions overall. Lots of rocks on the summit ridge, along with frozen sastrugis. Cautious skiing required.

reports.title: Dolomite Traverse Extravaganza
reports.comment: quick: Great day out with fast travel.  Crampons needed all of the way up from the Helen lake access side.  There is still a snow bridge to cross the Helen creek.  Some steeper exposed cramponing necessary. The ski down from Dolomite Pass is still well filled in through the tight canyon but will melt out fast.  The trees down to the car remained supportive to skiers.

reports.title: Wapta
reports.comment:
quick: 2 days on the wapta at the weekend summiting St Nic and Gordon. Unsettled weather for both days brought blue skies, heavy snowfall and intermittent whiteout conditions. No surprise that coverage is lacking somewhat compared to previous years however travel was fast and skiing was great especially down from st nic towards the hut. 

Saw one sz 2 Cornice failure on vulture peak NE aspect. Sus…

reports.title: Obsevation subpeak.
reports.comment: quick: Good freeze overnight, but breakable(2 or 3 cm thick) at 2000m improving to a solid crust st 2200m. Strong winds all day out of the sw, where loading ne Ridgeline features with wind slabs. Glacier had good wind pressed powder. Colouir at the bottom of the glacier had some wind slab in it so didn't go down very far.  South bowl had 1-2 cm of powder on a semi supportive variable crust made fo…

reports.title: Observation subpeak
reports.comment: quick: Decent freeze at 2000m, hard freeze above 2200m.  Good skiing on wind pressed snow on the glacier. South aspects were 1-2 cm of wind swept powder on a semi supportive crust was fun but challenging.  Trees had ski pen of 5 cm on slightly isothermic snow.  Winds were strong all day out of the SW creating wind slabs on NE Ridgeline features.

reports.title: Watermelon subpeak
reports.comment: quick: Great freeze overnight.  Very crusty in the morning made for some bootpackjng or ski crampons in steep areas. Good corn skiing on the solars and good power on Nw slopes above 2350m but was pin wheeling on us.  Compared to Friday the loose wet cycle was fairly quite a steady nw wind kept things from overheating. Skied up an outlier of watermelon a nice diversion from the Dolamite traverse wh…

reports.title: Mosquito Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Attempted Mosquito Mountain on Saturday. Turned around about 100m from the summit after a couple whumphs and not liking the look of a wind loaded start zone. Enjoyable snow on the ski down to the valley. Good coverage on the mosquito Creek trail. Photos of the surrounding area for reference.

reports.title: Noseeum South Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Coming from a camp in Mosquito Creek, we ascended South Molar Pass and Andromache Noseeum Col, before descending to Noseeum Lake and then down the Noseeum South Couloir. 

Great (firm) travel conditions around the back of Noseeum. South Molar Pass was straightforward, with a few bootpack steps due to the waterfall in the gully. Great (firm) travel conditions from South Molar to the ascent s…

reports.title: Cirque glacier
reports.comment: quick: Good freeze above 2200m.  Not much solar input but tempratures climbed through out the day and with some green houseing produced moist snow to 2850m on polar aspects.  Good corn skiing.  On our late exit at 5pm we found sticky but supportive snow below 2300m. Lots of wetloose on all aspects in the afternoon.
